findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13(B) Observed a container of chili to be thawing in the microwave. Microwave was not running and chili was sitting at room temperature within the device. The chili was still chilled, but not frozen. Educated on thawing during the inspection. Operator removed the chili from the microwave and began to reheat in a pan on the stovetop. 

Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

-Items in prep cooler #1 observed ~55F, including chopped lettuce and cut veggies. CORRECTED- Foods relocated to walk-in cooler to rapidly cool. Prep cooler will be serviced. Ensure equipment is holding temperature properly.
-An opened jug of salsa and an opened container of oil and vinegar dressing were observed in the dry storage area. Both items were labeled "Refrigerate after opening." CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC. Items were discarded.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16 (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (P)

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment: Damp wiping cloth observed on the counter between two prep coolers, not in solution. Wet wiping cloths must be stored submerged in a sanitizer solution. CORRECTED- Cloth was returned to sanitizer solution.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14 (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C)

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Employee washed hands, then turned faucet off without using a barrier to prevent recontamination of hands. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC and employee. Employee re-washed hands. Reference 2-301.12. (P)

Employee entered kitchen and donned gloves without washing hands. Employees must wash hands immediately before engaging in food prep and before donning gloves. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC and employee. Employee washed hands. Reference 2-301.14. (P)

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment: Employee used bare hands to plate slices of cake. Employees must prevent contamination from their hands by washing hands and using gloves to prevent bare hand contact with food. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC and employee. Employee washed hands and donned gloves to serve cake.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11 (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. (P)

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: No sanitizer detected from Cl sanitizing dish machine. CORRECTED- Employee was able to fix dish machine to dispense proper concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114 (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed on the manufacturer's label. (P)

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment: Two opened containers of heavy cream in the kitchen fridge and an opened gallon of milk in a prep cooler are without date markings. CORRECTED- PIC labeled foods with the dates they were opened.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17 Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). (Pf)

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment: Minestrone soup observed thawing on the kitchen counter. Foods must be thawed under refrigeration, completely submerged under cool running water, or for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready to eat foods to rise above 41F. CORRECTED- Soup was still solid when observed, and was relocated to the walk-in cooler to thaw. Reference 3-501.13. (C)

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment: Two dead cockroaches observed on glue traps-- one behind the bar near the cash register, and one under the ice machines. The premises shall be maintained free of insects, rodents and other pests. Eliminate pests, using proper pest control processes as needed. Reference 6-501.112. (C)

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: No sanitizer bucket made during food prep. CORRECTED- Sanitizer bucket was made to 200ppm Cl.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11 (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. (C)

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Date marking is not on an opened gallon of milk in the first prep cooler. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC. Milk was labeled with the date it was opened.
3-501.17 Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date).

Date of 11/7 marked on cooked pasta in the first prep cooler, and 11/3  on marinara sauce in the walk-in cooler exceed the time limit. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC. Foods were voluntarily discarded.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17 Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days.

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.comment: Baked potatoes are stored on top of the oven out of temperature control. Facility does not have a written Time as a Public Health Control policy. CORRECTED- Created written policy for using time as a control for baked potatoes.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.19 If time without temperature control is used as the public health control for READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD that is held for service (1) Written procedures shall be prepared in advance, maintained in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. (Pf)

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment: The method of cooling rice is inadequate. Observed rice on the top shelf of the walk-in cooler covered in plastic wrap, with a sealed lid at 135F (probed). Food must be uncovered during cooling, if protected from overhead contamination. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC. Rice was uncovered and labeled with the time. Advised PIC to monitor the cooling process.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.15 (A) Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of FOOD being cooled: (1) Placing the FOOD in shallow pans; (2) Separating the FOOD into smaller or thinner portions; (3)Using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT; (4) Stirring the FOOD in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods. (Pf)

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
Chili was observed thawing from frozen at room temperature. CORRECTED- Chili was placed in the walk-in cooler to thaw under refrigeration.
3-501.13 Time and temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41°F or less; or (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F or below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; or (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order.

Thawed fish observed still wrapped in reduced oxygen packaging (ROP) with a label indicating it must be removed from packaging before thawing. Thaw frozen fish according to manufacturer's instructions.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13 (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in ¶(A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in ¶ (B) of this section. (C)

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment: Two bottles of wine stored in ice to be used for consumption behind the bar. After use to cool food or other items, ice may not be used as food. CORRECTED- Beverages were removed from ice intended for service. Discussed with PIC.
findings.citation_text: 3-303.11 After use as a medium for cooling the exterior surfaces of FOOD such as melons or FISH, PACKAGED FOODS such as canned BEVERAGES, or cooling coils and tubes of EQUIPMENT, ice may not be used as FOOD. (P)

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 4-602.13  (C)  Observed soil residue present on fans in walk in cooler. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Observed soil residue present on inside of microwave. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the deli slicer to have some food debris from this morning prep. Make sure to wash, rinse and sanitize food contact surfaces after each use.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed a leak at the prep sink and three compartment sinks. Repair the leak.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
1) Observed corned beef dated for 04/10. Manager stated he cut it himself on Saturday, 04/21/18, and an employee improperly date marked it. 2) Observed chili dated 04/13 in the walk-in cooler. Upon further investigation, this product is frozen, then thawed. When doing this process the date the product was made, froze, and thawed, should be annotated on the product. Chili was pulled on 04/21/18. Facility was allowed to apply the correct date to the product. 
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed sauces (hollandaise, bearnaise, and BBQ) on the grill to be being held at temperatures ranging from 87F-107F when probed. Discussed proper hot holding with the manager and that the product should either be cold held or hot held. Product was timed for 4 hours after it was removed from temperature control for discard (3:30 PM discard). Ensure that products are properly temperature controlled. 
750-150(b)  Hot potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 135°F or above except during the cooling process. Store hot foods at 135°F or above. (Except for rare roast beef which may be held at 130F.)

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed raw pooled eggs being stored over RTE glazes. Ensure that raw products are stored below RTE foods. Eggs were moved during the inspection. 
750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.comment:
Observed multiple rotten/moldy potatoes in a box with other potatoes. The potatoes should be discarded once they show signs of spoilage, otherwise they can increase pest (drain flies) issues within the facility. Rotten potatoes were discarded during the inspection. 
750-100 Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
1) Observed raw pork and sliced deli meats in a cooler, next to an ice bath. The products were intended to be in the ice bath since the cooler is not working, but they were not. Manager states he had been utilizing Time as a Public Health Control for the items. The process he described was to pull the items out for 3-4 hours at a time, then put them back in the walk-in cooler to cool down again. The manager was advised that this is temperature abuse and this practice should cease. Time as a Public Health Control was explained to the manager and he stated he would rather start cold holding the products properly. Products were discarded during the inspection due to being at their time limit.  
750-153(a) Food shall not be held more that 4 hours past the point it is removed from temperature control. Do not hold food in excess of four hours after removal from temperature control.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.
750-250  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment:
Observed the facility's cooling practices to be out of control and unmonitored. Chili had been cooling since 11:30AM and was temperature checked at 3:30PM by the inspector. Chili was probed at 82F. The chili was being cooled in 1-2 gallon containers. Facility was instructed on proper cooling practices and provided with cooling logs. Facility reheated this product, as well as italian beef that was probed at 96F, after being placed in the cooler at 1:30 PM. Facility will do cooling logs and maintain them for a month at a time, then discard them. 
750-140(b)  Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.comment:
Observed potato with bacon soup thawing on top of the oven in the kitchen. This is an improper method and should be ceased. One of the methods below should be utilized when thawing PHFs. Soup was moved to walk-in for thawing. 
750-240 Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the  following method. 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under  potable running water 70°F or below or below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
1) Observed an employee leave the kitchen with a glove on, then return to the kitchen and attempt to continue prepping with the same glove still on. Ensure that any time tasks are switched or the cook leaves the kitchen, that the gloves are removed, hands are washed, and new gloves donned prior to restarting food handling. 2) Observed 2 employees wash their hands, then turn off the faucet without a barrier. Employees were stopped, educated, and instructed to rewash their hands. Ensure that the faucet is turned off with a barrier to avoid recontaminating hands. 
750-510d To avoid re-contaminating their hands, food employees shall use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a hand-washing sink or the handle of a restroom door.
750-510a Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed the facility to be using foil around their "insinkerator" to prevent water from spraying. Foil should not be used for this since it is not a smooth, easily cleanable surface. Manager states they are trying to get this piece of equipment replaced. Ensure that all non-food contact surfaces are smooth, easily cleanable and maintained in a clean state. 
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
1) Observed the dish washer to not test for sanitizer. Upon conveying this to the manager, he stated they were out of sanitizer. Ensure that the sanitizer is regularly checked to avoid using contaminated dishes in the facility. 2) Upon switching to a 3 compartment set-up, the sanitizer was tested after the dish washing had already started. The sanitizer was a 10 ppm Chlorine. If using chlorine, then the minimum concentration is 50 ppm for fully immersed dishes. The concentration was corrected with assistance from inspector. 
750-830 All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.
750-820d Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed an ice scoop at the bar stored with the handle in the ice. Ensure that the ice scoop is stored on a clean surface, or with the handle extending out of the ice. Ice scoop moved during the inspection. 
750-290 Ice scoop shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Observed a pan of utensils that had food debris in the bottom and on the utensils. Ensure that once utensils are stored clean they are maintained in an area that prevents them from becoming recontaminated. Entire pan, including utensils, sent to dish during the inspection. 
750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
Observed a hand sink without paper towels in the rear of the facility. Hand towels were provided during the inspection. Ensure that hand towels and soap are maintained at all hand sinks at all times. 
750-1120e A supply of soap and and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
During the follow up inspection it was noted that there were no FSSMC on site while food prep was being done. Ensure that more employees are sent through the FSSMC course to ensure that one is present at all times food prep is occurring. 
750-540 All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed 2 bulk bags of a white powder sitting on the shelf near the hand sink without any labeling. Ensure that if an item is removed from its original packaging that it is labeled with what it is. 
750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
1) Observed horseradish sauce, that is made in house, in the service cooler, in a tupperware container, without a date mark. Ensure that any PHFs are date marked with the date it was made and used within 7 days, or discarded. Owner was allowed to date mark the item stating it was made on 03/05/2017. 2) Observed half & half in the service cooler that had an exterior temperature of 62F on infrared. The half & half was probed at 52F. Ensure that refrigerated PHFs are maintained within the proper temperature. Owner states the half & half frequently goes between the service cooler and the counter. It is unsure when the item came out of temperature, but she states the rush began around 12:00 PM. The item was allowed to be time marked and used by 4:00 PM. 3) Observed the salad cooler, next to the chest freezer, to have salad dressings probed from 48F-52F. The lid was open upon inspector's arrival. Kitchen manager stated the lid was probably opened around 12:00 PM. Items were allowed to be time marked to be discarded at 4:00 PM. Ensure that all refrigerated PHFs are kept within their proper temperature, or time marked when they come out of temperature and used within 4 hours. 4) Observed the salad prep cooler, that is next to salad prep table, to have Caesar in it that was probed at 58F. Employee stated it had been placed in there at 11:00 AM from a container that was open and being held, in temperature, below the cooler. Ensure that all refrigerated PHFs are kept within their proper temperature, or time marked when they come out of temperature and used within 4 hours. Manager was allowed to time mark the Caesar for use before 3:00 PM. The item should be discarded at 3:00 PM. 
750-153(a) Food shall not be held more that 4 hours past the point it is removed from temperature control. Do not hold food in excess of four hours after removal from temperature control.
750-250  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed baked potatoes sitting on top of the oven. Manager stated they were removed from the oven at 11:00 AM. The baked potatoes were probed at temperatures of 84-110F. Manager was educated that baked potatoes are a potentially hazardous food and should be hot held, or time marked for discarding within 4 hours. If Time as Control is going to be used, then a written policy with SCDPH needs to be made. Potatoes were time marked to be discarded at 3:00 PM.
750-150(b)  Hot potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 135°F or above except during the cooling process. Store hot foods at 135°F or above. (Except for rare roast beef which may be held at 130F.)

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.comment:
Observed sliced roast beef sitting on the counter being thawed. Manager acknowledged that it had been there for approximately 1 hour. The food was still solid. The manager moved the item to the walk-in cooler to continue thawing. 
750-240 Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the  following method. 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under  potable running water 70°F or below or below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed the ice scoop at the bar being stored in a cup that was being stored inside the ice. Ice is considered food and only food contact surfaces should come into contact with the ice. Ice scoops may be stored in the ice or on a clean surface. Discussed placing ice scoop in cup next to the ice bin is also appropriate. 
750-290 Ice scoop shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed a tall cooler in the rear of the facility, by the ice machines, that has the seal in disrepair. Ensure that the seal is repaired or replaced to provide a smooth, easily cleanable surface. 
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
Observed 2 sanitizer buckets during the inspection that were not at the proper concentration. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are regularly remade during busy times of service. The proper concentration should be at 100 ppm. Buckets were remade during the inspection. 
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed lines in the bar cooler for the keg that had mold growing on them. The coolers have a regular accumulations of water, as stated by bartender and owner. This will only increase molds growth within this area. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are cleaned regularly and kept free of dust, dirt, and other debris. 
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed both bar cabinet coolers, used for kegs, to have an accumulation of standing water in the bases. Owner states this is a normal occurence and that they clean the water out regularly. There are containers of food stored in one of the chest coolers (olives). This poses a potential for cross contamination and the units should be serviced to ensure water does not accumulate in the base of them. 
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment:
Observed 6+ drain flies in the mop sink room. Manager and owner state that cleaning has increased, but it has become a recent issue over the past year. There were also drain flies noted in the kitchen (2), but not in as great of numbers. Ensure that effective measures are used to minimize drain flies within the facility. 
750-1160 Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.comment:
Observed a potato in a box with other potatoes that was rotting on an edge. Ensure that food is in a sound condition and disposed of if it is not. Potato was discarded immediately. 
750-100 Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed milk in a prep cooler in the kitchen that was opened, but not date marked. Ensure that potentially hazardous dairy products are date marked and maintained at the proper temperatures. Employee stated the milk was opened the night before and he date marked it at this time. 
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed raw chicken stored with made to eat sandwhiches. Ensure that raw and ready to eat foods are stored separately or apart from each other. Raw chicken was moved at this time. 
750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed seals on a cabinet cooler at the bar to be soiled with a black substance. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are maintained clean and free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, and debris. 
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment:
Observed flies in the dry storage area, next to the soda syrup rack, and in the bar area. Ensure that measures are being taken to control flies, such as cleaning drains and disposing of spoiled food. Facility was notified to clean drains and have Century make an extra visit. 
750-1160 Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed the following floor areas to be in disrepair or soiled: 1) The coving near the dish area was noted to be tearing away from the wall. 2) The metal coving by the dish table was pulled signiificantly away from the wall. 3) The drain under the soda syrup rack was noted to be filled with rags. Ensure that these areas are maintained in good repair, smooth, and easily cleanable. Recaulk the dish coving and fix the metal coving. Remove the rags from the soda syrup rack and clean the drain. 
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed the area between the hoods to have grease forming droplets in this area. Ensure that this area is also being cleaned during weekly cleaning of the hood. 
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Lighting provided as required.  Fixtures shielded
findings.comment:
Observed the light shields in the kitchen to be chipping or missing end caps. Replace the light shields to broke light shields within the kitchen. 
750-1240 All lights in the food prep, food storage or kitchen area of a establishment must be properly shielded (i.e. either have a physical shield or be a shatter resistant bulb) so as to reduce the potential for cross contamination in case of breakage.  Provide properly shielded lights.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 140: The cooler holding burgers and crab cakes is observed holding foods at 50F (probed crab cakes and mango salsa). Foods were recently placed into the preparation cooler (after lunch). The foods were allowed to be moved. Cooler is not going to be used until it can be serviced. Crowder is being called to service. Will spot check on Tuesday to insure working preparation cooler. There are two additional preparation coolers present.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: 820: The dish machine is not dispensing sanitizing solution. Machine was primed and nothing dispensed. MJ Kellner was out earlier in the week. Kellner was called during the inspection to service. Discussed using the dish machine for wash and rinse and then using the sink for sanitizing. Will spot check on Tuesday.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
